english.html: of which this du Tilh stood convicted, besides the ordinary blasphemies which this rogue habitually used, as we have made amply to appear above, where also the penalty of blasphemers has been spoken of <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup>.

notes.citation: Coras's own Annotation XXXVI (annot-036), on blasphemy and its penalty

english.html: For the offence done principally to God, in violating the holy estate of marriage, which God has above all honoured and sanctified by the presence of his son Jesus Christ, performing the first miracle, saying to his Apostles a2 [unclear: the clause breaks off here in the print; no words of Christ follow]: it was also fitting that the reparation of this prodigious crime should begin with public penance (amende honorable) before the temple and the house of God b.

notes.citation: John 2 (2:1–11, the marriage at Cana, Christ's first miracle)
Isaiah 56 (56:7, "my house shall be called a house of prayer"); Matthew 21 (21:13, the same words in the cleansing of the temple)
notes.original: Eſaye c. lvj. S. Math. xxi.

english.html: The Court had at one time resolved that the public penance (amende honorable) should also be made at the bar of the audience chamber (parquet de l'audience), on the day of the pronouncing of the decision. But afterwards it was considered that this rash fellow was of a shameless impudence and an immeasurable overweening, presumptuous, virulent, and more abounding in petulance of language than a Theon or an Archilochus, and that he would at every word have disturbed Monsieur the president who was pronouncing, and the assembly: wherefore it was on the contrary resolved, for this sole reason, that they would content themselves with the penance which should be made at the place of Artigat, where he had offended.

High justice is what the Jurisconsults call MERE IMPERE [merum imperium, pure power], that is to say a sovereign power of the sword, and of punishing anyone corporally by whipping of the body, cutting off of limbs, or, if
